inputs.label: Report recipient email
inputs.description: Where daily reports and alerts are emailed (defaults to the owner)

inputs.label: Low-stock threshold (days)
inputs.description: Flag a SKU when projected days of stock left falls below this

inputs.label: Reorder lead time (days)
inputs.description: How long a restock takes — used to project stockouts

inputs.label: Stuck-order window (hours)
inputs.description: Flag orders still in processing/pending past this many hours

inputs.label: Include analytics context
inputs.description: Pull sessions and conversion rate to explain sales changes

inputs.label: Product review window (days)
inputs.description: Lookback window for the product performance review

activities.intent: Read the last 32 days of orders, with totals, refunds, discounts and lines, from the store connection; it resolves whichever platform the company runs

Compute yesterday's charged, gross and net revenue, refunds, discount load, order count and AOV, each beside the prior day, the prior same weekday and the trailing 30-day daily average, and the top movers up and down. Any figure the store cannot return is null and named in notAvailable, never estimated.
Add traffic and conversion context to explain the day's sales movement
steps: If {{inputs.use_analytics}} is no, or no analytics connection is bound, answer {"skipped": true} and stop

Read sessions, users and ecommerce conversion rate for {{nodes.pull-sales.day}}, the prior day, the prior same weekday and the trailing 30 days through analytics.metric.series and analytics.metric.get
Compare those trends against the sales deltas in {{nodes.pull-sales.deltaPct}}
Diagnose any revenue change as fewer visitors versus a lower conversion rate and state which
Answer only JSON: {"skipped": false, "sessions": {...}, "conversion": {...}, "diagnosis": "..."}; if analytics is unavailable answer {"skipped": true, "reason": "..."} rather than blocking the report

activities.intent: Compile and deliver the daily sales report with movers and a watch list
steps: Build the headline line from {{nodes.pull-sales.current}}: revenue, orders and AOV, each with its delta from {{nodes.pull-sales.deltaPct}} and the comparison basis. Quote the computed figures; never recompute or estimate one, and say "not available from this store" for each item in {{nodes.pull-sales.notAvailable}}
List the top movers up and down from {{nodes.pull-sales.moversUp}} and {{nodes.pull-sales.moversDown}} with their numbers
Fold in the traffic context from the previous step to explain the day's direction in one read; leave it out if it was skipped
Write the single most important action for the day as a one-line read; if the day is clean and within normal range, write a one-line all-clear instead of padded sections
Send the report with mail.message.send to {{inputs.report_recipient}}, or to the owner when it is blank
Emit report.ready with the headline metrics and mover lists

activities.intent: Read the order pipeline of the last 30 days, every state, with payment and fulfillment status and tracking, from the store connection

Flag orders stuck in processing or pending past stuck_processing_hours and on hold past 72 hours, paid orders with no fulfillment or tracking past the same window, failed and uncaptured payments, recent refunds and chargebacks, and repeated failed attempts from one customer. Ages and thresholds are computed here; an order state the store cannot return is named in notAvailable, never inferred.
Go on only when the scan found an issue; an empty scan ends the run silently.
Read the order alert log kept from the last alert
steps: Recall the memory "store alert log: orders"
Answer only JSON: {"alerted": "<the logged key=tier pairs, exactly as stored, or an empty string>"}

activities.intent: Apply the alert cooldown in code: an issue already reported is not flagged again while it stays open, unless it crossed a worse threshold.
Alert only when an issue is new or worse; otherwise the run ends silently.
Notify the owner of new order issues with full context
steps: Work from {{nodes.cooldown.alerts}}: sort by impact, oldest stuck orders and highest-value failed payments first, quoting each computed age and amount
Summarize each issue with order ID, state, age, customer, amount and the likely cause
Group issues by type so stuck orders, failed payments and unfulfilled paid orders are clearly separated, and say "not available from this store" for each item in {{nodes.scan-pipeline.notAvailable}}
Email the alert with mail.message.send to {{inputs.report_recipient}}, or to the owner when it is blank
Save {{nodes.cooldown.log}} to memory as "store alert log: orders", replacing the previous entry
Emit order.issue with the alerted issue list so a support or fulfillment agent can intervene

activities.intent: No order is stuck, failed or unfulfilled; the next scan reads the pipeline again.

params.command: echo '{"summary": "No order is stuck, failed or unfulfilled; the next scan reads the pipeline again."}'

activities.intent: Every open order issue was already alerted and none got worse; the next scan reads them again.

params.command: echo '{"summary": "Every open order issue was already alerted and none got worse; the next scan reads them again."}'

activities.intent: Read current stock per SKU and variant from the store connection; it resolves whichever platform the company runs
Read the last 30 days of orders for sell-through
Keep the stock list in a per-run file so the projection can join it with the sales.

Compute a trailing daily sell-through per SKU and days of stock left, flag any SKU projected to hit zero before reorder_lead_time_days or below low_stock_days, and rank by velocity-weighted urgency so fast movers outrank slow movers.
Go on only when a SKU crossed a line; otherwise the run ends silently.
Read the stock alert log kept from the last alert
steps: Recall the memory "store alert log: stock"
Answer only JSON: {"alerted": "<the logged key=tier pairs, exactly as stored, or an empty string>"}

activities.intent: Apply the alert cooldown in code: an unchanged low-stock SKU is not re-alerted while it stays low, only when it gets worse.
Alert only when a SKU is newly low or worse; otherwise the run ends silently.
Notify the owner of SKUs approaching stockout
steps: Format {{nodes.cooldown.alerts}} sorted by soonest-to-zero, quoting each computed days left, on hand and units per day
Call out every SKU marked reorderNow as a hard reorder-now flag: it stocks out before a restock can land
Say "not available from this store" for each item in {{nodes.project-stock.notAvailable}}
Email the alert with mail.message.send to {{inputs.report_recipient}}, or to the owner when it is blank
Save {{nodes.cooldown.log}} to memory as "store alert log: stock", replacing the previous entry
Emit inventory.low with SKU, current stock, days of stock left and velocity for an ordering agent

activities.intent: No SKU is under the low-stock line or inside the restock lead time; the next check reads stock again.

params.command: echo '{"summary": "No SKU is under the low-stock line or inside the restock lead time; the next check reads stock again."}'

activities.intent: Every low SKU was already alerted and none got worse; the next check reads stock again.

params.command: echo '{"summary": "Every low SKU was already alerted and none got worse; the next check reads stock again."}'

activities.intent: Read the review_window_days input once and work out how far back to read: the window and the equal window before it.
Read per-product sales for the review window and the prior equal window from the store connection
Read the catalog with unit cost where the store carries it
Read current stock per SKU
Keep the catalog in a per-run file for the ranking.
Keep the stock list in a per-run file for the ranking.

Compute units and revenue per product for the current window and the prior equal window; rank top performers with trend, decliners that sold last period and dropped sharply, dead stock with inventory and zero sales, and contribution margin where cost exists. Any per-product figure the store cannot return is null and named in notAvailable.
Add product-level traffic and conversion context where analytics is available
steps: If {{inputs.use_analytics}} is no, or no analytics connection is bound, answer {"skipped": true} and stop

Read product or landing-page sessions and conversion over the last {{nodes.window.days}} days through analytics.page.metrics and analytics.metric.series, for the products in {{nodes.rank-products.performers}} and {{nodes.rank-products.decliners}}
Flag products with high traffic but low conversion as merchandising or pricing problems
Flag declining products whose drop is explained by lost traffic versus lost conversion

Answer only JSON: {"skipped": false, "products": [{"sku": "...", "sessions": 0, "conversion": 0, "read": "..."}]}; if analytics is unavailable answer {"skipped": true, "reason": "..."} without blocking the review

activities.intent: Compile and deliver the weekly product performance review
steps: Lead with the top performers from {{nodes.rank-products.performers}} and, where cost exists, {{nodes.rank-products.byMargin}}, quoting the computed revenue, units, margin and change
Surface the decliners in {{nodes.rank-products.decliners}} as the priority section, since they are the silent revenue leaks

List the dead stock in {{nodes.rank-products.deadStock}} with the computed value tied up ({{nodes.rank-products.deadStockValueCents}} cents in all), and say "not available from this store" for each item in {{nodes.rank-products.notAvailable}}
Fold in the traffic context from the previous step to diagnose decliners and underperformers; leave it out if it was skipped
Recommend concrete actions: promote, discount to clear, reorder, or retire
Send the review with mail.message.send to {{inputs.report_recipient}}, or to the owner when it is blank
Emit report.ready with the ranked lists and recommended actions

activities.intent: Read the last 32 days of orders from the store connection; it resolves whichever platform the company runs
Read current stock per SKU
Keep the stock list in a per-run file so the projection can join it with the sales.
Today's running revenue, order count and AOV, each against the same point of the prior day, the prior same weekday and the 30-day average.
Every order currently stuck, failed or paid and unfulfilled.
Days of stock left for the SKUs under the line, fastest movers first.
Give an on-demand snapshot of sales, open issues, and low stock right now
steps: Sales headline from {{nodes.sales-now.current}} with its deltas from {{nodes.sales-now.deltaPct}} and the comparison basis
Open issues: {{nodes.issues-now.count}} in all, with the worst offenders from {{nodes.issues-now.issues}}
Low stock: the SKUs in {{nodes.stock-now.flagged}} by days left
Quote the computed figures only; say "not available from this store" for each item in {{nodes.sales-now.notAvailable}}, {{nodes.issues-now.notAvailable}} and {{nodes.stock-now.notAvailable}}
Sort every section by impact and finish with the single most important action right now
If everything is within normal range, return a concise all-clear
